title: Add sequence-length-aware traffic synthesizer and profile-guided baseline collector
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Existing workload runners sample request shapes uniformly or by hand-curated mixes which misses temporal correlations (sequence length bursts, conversational rollups) observed in customer telemetry. This PR adds a sequenced traffic synthesizer and a profile-guided baseline collector to produce representative, reproducible workloads for latency and KV cache profiling.

What this PR does (single-string summary):
- Introduces `temporal_correlated_runner.py`: a new workload runner that replays synthetic sessions with configurable sequence-length autocorrelation and inter-request timing distributions. Supports seedable RNG for repeatable runs.
- Adds `profiles/guided_sampler.py`: profile-guided input sampler that consumes production histograms (token count, prompt prefixes, user-session lengths) and generates weighted samples to exercise long-tail and bursty patterns.
- Adds `profiles/baselines/*`: stored canonical baselines (JSON) for short/medium/long conversational workloads and a README describing how to generate/validate them.
- Adds `reporters/provenance_delta.py`: an enrichment layer for the existing reporter pipeline that annotates aggregated deltas with profile provenance and sample counts to help root-cause SLO regressions.
- Small test harness and CI workflow updates: unit tests for sampler, an integration test that runs a short synthetic replay in the benchmark container, and a flakiness guard for timing-dependent tests.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Temporal correlation model: an AR(1)-like mechanism was chosen (configurable rho) instead of full HMM to keep generation cheap and interpretable. This is sufficient to reproduce burstiness seen in telemetry while keeping runtime overhead low.
- Profile-guided sampling prioritizes tail coverage: sampler supports a "tail_weight" parameter which increases sampling probability for rare long sequences to ensure regressions are caught early. This increases average test cost but improves regression sensitivity.
- Determinism: the runner exposes a `--seed` flag and dumps RNG state to the run metadata to make replays reproducible.

Testing and results summary:
- Unit tests: 18 new tests covering sampler distribution, RNG determinism, and provenance annotations.
- Integration run: a short run (1000 simulated tokens across mixed sessions) executed on CI container showed negligible added overhead to runner startup (<40ms) and produced expected delta annotations.
- Local perf run (nvme rig): using the new runner with baseline profile `baselines/conv-long.json` surfaced a 7.2% median tail latency increase on a quantized model variant; this surfaced a batching/KV-cache regression that the runtime team fixed in a follow-up.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests added [x] Integration test added [x] README and baseline artifacts included [x] Linear tasks linked [x] CI green after re-run

Commits summary (high level, single string):
- 8 commits: initial scaffold for runner and sampler, add baseline JSONs, implement provenance reporter, add unit tests, add integration harness, CI workflow tweaks, fix flakiness in timing test, address reviewer feedback.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on sampler weighting logic and the provenance schema (reporters/provenance_delta.py) — we want to make sure the provenance annotations are stable and won't explode cardinality in downstream dashboards.
- The AR(1) model is intentionally simple; we can extend to more complex temporal models later if customers require it.

Follow-ups (planned):
- ENG-1178: Add adaptive sampling that adjusts tail_weight based on recent regression alerts.
- ENG-1210: Add CDF-driven validators to automatically gate model rollouts when baseline deltas exceed thresholds.

Merge rationale and method: squash-and-merge after CI green and approval. The change set is additive (new artifacts) with small changes to existing CI workflow and no production runtime code modifications.
